meta.title: Workload Rebalancing Dashboard | Sāra 0002 | TriSaar Consulting
meta.description: Sāra 0002 case study in Insurance: an Excel and VBA workload rebalancing dashboard that gives operations leaders a self-service view of account-level effort, capacity and workload imbalance across offices.
meta.author: TriSaar Consulting

data.text: A self-service Excel and VBA dashboard that gives operations leaders a live view of workload, capacity and account-level effort across offices.
Workload management tool that helps leaders identify pressure points, test allocation scenarios, and rebalance work before teams become overloaded.

data.title: Turning account-level effort into a proactive management tool.
data.subtitle: A self-service dashboard that helped operations leaders see where workload was building up, test rebalancing scenarios and act before someone became overloaded.

pillars.label: Challenge
pillars.title: Invisible workload imbalance driving burnout & attrition.
pillars.body: Operations spanned over 15 offices and roughly 75 managers, executives and underwriters. But the workload was assigned informally, with no shared way to compare effort across people or operarions.

points.text: No standardized measure of 'workload' existed across operations
No unified view per person or account
Lack of early warning system to rebalance proactively

pillars.label: Solution
pillars.title: Self-service dashboard built for the Team that owns it.
pillars.body: We designed and built a workload dashboard in Excel VBA, that draws on the client's existing capacity model & benchmarks at global and local level, gives managers a visual way to see and rebalance assignments.

pillars.label: Impact
pillars.title: Reactive firefighting to Proactive rebalancing.
pillars.body: For the first time, operations leaders could see workload imbalance in one place, and act on it before it became a service or retention issue.

parts.text: We didn't just flag where workload was imbalanced, we gave the client's own team a
way to see and fix it, turning a recurring pain point into an operating habit.

data.title: Workload was visible in pieces, but not as a management system.
data.body: Operations spanned more than 15 offices and roughly 75 managers, executives and underwriters. Account ownership and expected effort existed in the underlying Excel model, but there was no simple, shared dashboard for operations leaders to see workload distribution, identify emerging pressure points or test how changes would affect capacity.

core.label: The Core Challenge
core.body: The data needed to manage workload already existed. The gap was turning account-level effort and working hours into a practical view that leaders could use to rebalance work.

points.title: Effort varied by account and role
points.body: Workload was not simply a count of accounts. Each account carried an expected working-hour requirement by role, creating different effort profiles across assignments.

points.title: Assignments drove capacity
points.body: The model needed to connect each account's required effort with the people and roles working on it to understand the resulting workload.

points.title: No easy scenario view
points.body: Operations leaders needed to test changes—not just observe the current state. Adding or removing people and accounts could materially change the workload balance.

points.title: Rebalancing was reactive
points.body: Without a practical management view, workload could build up before leaders had a clear way to identify where intervention was needed.

impact.label: The Business Impact
impact.body: Leaders had less visibility into emerging overload and fewer practical ways to evaluate alternative workload allocations before acting.

data.title: From an existing Excel model to a self-service workload cockpit.
data.intro: Rather than replacing the client's existing Excel model, we used it as the engine for a management dashboard. VBA processed the model's account-level effort, role requirements and assignments, then translated the results into a visual interface where operations leaders could inspect workload and test rebalancing scenarios.

hub.label: Our Approach
hub.body: Turn existing capacity data into a practical decision tool without forcing the team onto a new platform.

steps.title: Model workload at account level
steps.body: Used the existing Excel model to represent the working hours required for each account by role.

steps.title: Connect effort to assignments
steps.body: Linked the effort required by each account to the people and roles currently working on it, creating a workload view that reflected actual assignments.

steps.title: Automate the dashboard with VBA
steps.body: Built VBA logic to process the Excel model and present the resulting workload information through a dashboard, keeping the workflow inside the team's existing environment.

steps.title: Enable scenario-based rebalancing
steps.body: Designed the tool so leaders could test changes to the operating model, including adding or removing people and accounts, and see how those changes affected workload distribution before making a decision.

items.title: One operating view
items.body: Operations leaders could assess workload across offices from one dashboard.

items.title: Test before changing
items.body: Leaders could evaluate alternative allocations before moving people or accounts.

items.title: Self-service ownership
items.body: The solution remained within the team's existing Excel environment rather than creating vendor dependency.

enablers.label: Key Enablers
enablers.intro: The solution combined existing business logic with lightweight automation.

data.title: See imbalance earlier. Test options. Rebalance before overload.
data.intro: The dashboard changed workload management from a reactive exercise into a repeatable decision process for operations leaders.

orbit.label: Business Impact
orbit.tagline: A clearer, more proactive way to manage workload.
